proposed_from.topic: Nuisance-uniform minimax outcome annotation for an overlapping finite causal-policy menu. In a finite-stratum binary-treatment model with known propensities, a frozen rank-full menu of at least three overlapping policies, budgeted outcome-acquisition rates bounded away from zero, and unrestricted eta-positive probabilities on a fixed finite outcome support, derive the local Gaussian policy-contrast experiment uniformly over the full Qh+Nu treatment-effect fiber and every outcome-shape nuisance tangent. Characterize the minimax welfare-regret value V* over deterministic limiting annotation designs; give certified finite-grid upper and lower computation; and construct a vanishing-pilot, stabilized design selector, joint AIPW contrast estimator, and Gaussian minimax rule attaining V*. For the stated rational three-policy witness with H=[-1,1]^2, prove that the unique minimizer of maximum pairwise contrast variance has regret above 0.1965 while a feasible design has regret below 0.18453, and extend the strict separation to an explicit open parameter neighborhood. Consumer: prospective independent validation of the eight azithromycin rules in the ABCD trial, where targeted follow-up replaces uniform or exogenous outcome collection. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: A saturated mean/shape decomposition gives orthogonal Fisher information and T_r' I_r T_r=Sigma(r)^(-1); bounded likelihood-ratio arguments support the full-nuisance lower-risk transfer. A projected nested-cell selector handles nonunique optima, and exact conditional AIPW covariance plus rectangle-risk transfer support attainment. Outward-rounded Arb certificates verify L(r_alt)<0.18453, L(r_G)>0.1965 and separation on a radius-10^-6 neighborhood. Tests covered shape nuisances, pilot information, discontinuous selectors, boundary minima, zero-regret sets, variance degeneracy, and current policy-design collisions. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Complete a measurable implementation theorem coupling the certified nested-cell design sieve and Gaussian observation-grid selector, with locally uniform risk attainment and deterministic optimal-rate convergence at every nonunique optimum. EARLY KILL TEST: Verify nested-cell stabilization at separated tied minima and a dyadic-boundary minimum under uniform approximation errors; failure to stabilize every fixed tree prefix stops universal attainment. proposed_from.novelty_justification: Gaussian games, three-action choice, and minimax treatment decisions with missing outcomes are not claimed as new. The new observation geometry is prospective and controlled: investigators randomize acquisition of treatment--stratum outcomes, while terminal actions are overlapping linear policy values. This yields a design-indexed non-diagonal covariance and a nuisance kernel containing every value-preserving outcome-shape direction. Relative to Higbee (2026), the theorem-level delta is exact: the rational witness has a three-way local tie and fourteen selective-annotation nuisance coordinates, violating the comparator's unique strongly concave smooth optimum conditions. Relative to Manski and Stoye, the outcomes remain point identified under known randomized treatment and annotation probabilities, and the annotation law is the design variable rather than an exogenous source of partial identification. The proposed deterministic-limit envelope is tied to an explicit conditional LAN and finite-prior transfer statement, then paired with an open measurable implementation question at nonunique and boundary optima. The rational witness adds a positive geometric theorem using only its internally defined probe: the singleton \(G_{\omega_0}\)-optimizer has regret above \(0.1965\), the displayed feasible design is below \(0.18453\), and the inequality persists on an explicit neighborhood.

seed_details.question: Can the local asymptotic minimax value for choosing among overlapping policies be characterized jointly with the outcome-annotation design, uniformly over all contrast-preserving outcome-shape directions, and attained by one feasible pilot procedure?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the scalar efficient welfare contrast in the limit experiment by the projection of the saturated cell-probability score onto the full vector of overlapping policy contrasts, with the annotation rate inside the information matrix.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for \(\text{policy annotation}+\text{minimax regret}\), \(\text{overlapping policies}+\text{Gaussian design}\), and \(\text{design-dependent covariance}+\text{policy regret}\) found scalar causal annotation, independent-arm best-arm identification, and smooth Bayes policy design, but no result with this joint object.
seed_details.ambition_reason: The kernel combines a nuisance-uniform limit experiment, a design-level minimax value, feasible attainment, and a robust strict separation; it does not claim the generality needed for a flagship result.

proposed_from.literature_map: Hirano and Porter (2009) provide the local Gaussian decision bridge for statistical treatment rules, but their efficient statistic concerns one binary welfare contrast under a fixed experiment. Masten (2023) treats many mutually exclusive treatments and computational games, while Kato (2026) obtains exact sequential best-arm constants for independently sampled arm means. Higbee (2026) gives a general two-wave Bayes design representation for smooth, strongly convex policy problems. Hu et al. (2024) optimize minimax-regret sample allocation when subgroup decisions and Gaussian signals separate. Nwankwo, Goldkind, and Zhou (2026) optimize costly outcome annotation for scalar ATE variance, and Wang, Wang, and Miao (2026) optimize componentwise semiparametric efficiency for vector parameters. Levis et al. (2024) supply the observed-data influence-function projection under double sampling, while Cook, Mishler, and Ramdas (2024) supply adaptive AIPW limit theory once probabilities stabilize. Luedtke and van der Laan (2016) show why nonunique optimal decisions are nonregular. Codi et al. (2025) estimate a joint covariance for competing clinical rules, and Kim et al. (2025) provide the azithromycin validation consumer. The unoccupied intersection is deterministic-limit minimax outcome annotation for correlated overlapping policy values, with transfer uniform over a saturated shape-nuisance fiber, tie-stable implementation, certified computation, and a robust separation from maximum-pairwise-variance design.
